I1.quote: High pressure hydrogen adsorption measurement was performed at −196 °C up to 100 bar on about 0.2 g sample. A high pressure volumetric BELSORP-HP apparatus was used to quantify the Gibbs excess amount of hydrogen adsorbed.
I1.location: main, p. 23895 (PDF page 3), Section 2.3 Hydrogen storage measurements at ambient and high pressure

I2.quote: The second weight loss of 82% with a valley at about 621 °C in the DTG curve took place between 400 and 750 °C, which was the result of combusting carbon in air. At 750 °C, the residual mass was below 1 wt%.
I2.location: main, p. 23895 (PDF page 3), Section 3 Results and discussion, TG-DTG of the HPCDCM (Fig. 2); the H2 sample is the carbide-derived carbon monolith HPCDCM (title, abstract)

I3.quote: The HPCDCM exhibited a good hydrogen uptake of 2.4 wt% at −196 °C and 1 bar. At high pressure, a saturated hydrogen uptake of up to 4.4 wt% was obtained at 36 bar and −196 °C
I3.location: main, p. 23898 (PDF page 6), Section 4 Conclusions; also Fig. 8a,b axes (H2 uptake vs pressure, −196 °C)

I4.quote: The surface area (2933 m2 g−1) and pore volume (2.101 cm3 g−1) of the HPCDCM are significantly increased compared to those of the OMSCM.
I4.location: main, p. 23896 (PDF page 4), Section 3 Results and discussion and Table 2 (HPCDCM, SBET 2933 m2 g-1); BET method p/p0 = 0.05-0.2 in Section 2.2, p. 23894

I5.quote: Hierarchical porous carbide-derived carbon monoliths (HPCDCM) were prepared by selective extraction of silicon from ordered mesoporous silicon carbide monoliths (OMSCM) through chlorination at high temperature.
I5.location: main, p. 23893 (PDF page 1), Abstract, first sentence

notes: Volumetric (Sieverts-type, BELSORP-HP) and Autosorb 1C H2 isotherms at -196 C on the HPCDCM; no retraction flag in record.json; paper reports its own H2 data (not a review); no statement that its H2 values were published before.
